sample.notes: Counts are the printed people analyzed for this contrast. Counts are not inferred from study-wide totals or degrees of freedom. Higher means greater semantic alignment with the fixed expert benchmark, a performance proxy. This is not similarity among experimental participants and is not interpreted as reduced creativity or increased participant homogeneity. The GPT coefficient is the GPT-versus-Control simple contrast in the factorial model, not the average effect of access across both training conditions. The regression uses all experimental arms. n_total is null because a total for the named pair of arms is not printed; the full model N is preserved in regression.model and the Observations source. Full-sample descriptive statistics are preserved verbatim in the Table A.7 source, without substituting them for arm means or SDs. SEs cluster on the intersection of mother tongue, high-school type and class, not on randomized class alone; they do not satisfy the assignment-class precision requirement for pooling. Graph coordinates and confidence-interval endpoints are not transcribed or estimated. Arm-specific analyzed counts are null because the arms of the responses missing within-solution diversity are not reported; initial arm counts are not reused for this reduced analysis. This is a full-sample model specification conditional on post-treatment response features, not an additional independent experiment or the unadjusted total effect of AI access. se_basis=participant records the single participant-level observation used in each regression; it does not certify valid precision for class randomization. The reported smaller clustering cells leave dependence across students in the same randomized class unaccounted for. Retain the printed SEs as reported results, but do not pool them as assignment-class precision. higher_is=more_similar is the literal direction of the expert-reference cosine-similarity outcome. It is retained as with_ai/other, not across_people/diversity; this direction must not be interpreted as evidence that the participants became less creative.

sample.notes: Counts are the people in the authors' posted data used for this contrast. Counts are not inferred from study-wide totals or degrees of freedom. Full-sample contrast of assignment to AI access, retaining participants who did not use it. The incentive indicators were assigned experimental factors. The paper prints no pooled AI or No-AI means or SDs; regression intercepts are not entered as arm means. The Table 5 omnibus F statistic and its p-value test the whole model and are not entered as the AI contrast. Counts for the AI and No-AI samples are explicitly printed in Table 2 and the full-sample outcome count in Table 5. se_basis describes the reported participant-level robust OLS analysis; whether session-level randomization requires different uncertainty remains unresolved. Although the authors call DAT baseline creative potential, the questionnaire follows the experimental stages and AI access ends with the composition. This is an immediate, same-session after_ai outcome; no elapsed interval is printed. No exact or bounded p-value for the AI coefficient is printed.

sample.notes: Counts are the printed people analyzed for this contrast. Counts are not inferred from study-wide totals or degrees of freedom. This is the full-sample Method main effect from the two-way Problem by Method ANOVA. The Table 2 Total rows are unadjusted descriptive summaries pooling different proportions of the problem groups; they are not printed as adjusted arm levels for this Method test. Following the screening correction, these summaries are preserved in the count quotation but are not entered as this test’s means or SDs or as a separate effect-size record. The paper prints no adjusted arm means, signed Method difference, SE, CI, or standardized effect. The F test alone does not identify direction. The counts were rechecked in the nonparenthesized Table 2 entries: n_treatment = 63, n_control = 51, n_total = 114. The smaller parenthesized counts belong to the self-report survey. The agreed fields were independently checked: question = with_ai and outcome_with_ai = true because LLM assistance was available during production of the scored solution (PDF p. 5, printed p. 511, Section 3.3). construct = usefulness because this is a design-quality composite of feasibility, requirements, innovativeness, and elaboration, not a separately reported novelty score (PDF pp. 4–5, printed pp. 510–511, Section 3.2.2). higher_is = more_creative denotes better design quality in the codebook’s usefulness construct. unit = participant and se_basis = participant because each student supplied one final solution, with expert scores averaged before the ANOVA; n_units remains null because n_total already counts the people. within_person = null because each student solved one problem under one assigned method (PDF p. 4, printed p. 510, Section 3.2.1). The common practice task was explicitly excluded from analysis. The outcome is immediate; no delayed unassisted output was assessed. comparison_type = ai_vs_active because the TRIZ-C control received the non-AI TRIZ contradiction-matrix aid through triz40.com; both arms using TRIZ does not make the control unassisted (PDF p. 5, printed p. 511, Section 3.3; creativity-codebook.md, Section 5). The authors flag unequal variances and potentially liberal F tests (PDF p. 6, printed p. 512, Section 4.2). Design quality addresses RQ1 (PDF p. 2, printed p. 508); no preregistration is stated. No numerical effect, count, or uncertainty has been derived.

sample.notes: Counts are the people in the authors' posted data used for this contrast. Counts are not inferred from study-wide totals or degrees of freedom. The analysis is at the rating level. Analyzed writer counts and pairwise totals are transcribed from Supplement Table S1; the combined-AI count uses the printed total for the two AI arms, without addition or subtraction. The supplement prints regression SEs and Human-only intercept estimates with their SEs. Neither document prints rating-level or participant-level SDs for this outcome or numerical confidence-interval endpoints. Supplement Table S3 supplies the component coefficient and SE. The component analyses were preregistered as robustness tests, not primary tests (Supplement Section 9, question 5). Item wording is available in Supplement Section 1 and the evaluator screenshots in Section 8. No number is estimated from a figure. The rating code is used because the schema has no evaluator category; it does not assert that the paper treated every rating as independent. Treatment means are not computed from the constant and coefficient. Existing main-text p-values are retained. For otherwise missing p-values, significance symbols supply the printed upper bound and an unmarked coefficient leaves p_value null. The multi-regressor F-Stat is an omnibus model test and is not entered as a test of either individual AI-arm contrast.

sample.notes: Counts are the printed people analyzed for this contrast. Counts are not inferred from study-wide totals or degrees of freedom. Each writer contributes one story; the paper specifies OLS with robust SEs for writer-study outcomes (PDF p. 8), so se_basis is participant. n_units is the printed total of stories in the full three-arm analysis, not a printed pairwise subtotal. Analyzed writer counts and pairwise totals are transcribed from Supplement Table S1; the combined-AI count uses the printed total for the two AI arms, without addition or subtraction. The supplement supplies the robust regression SE and the Human-only intercept SE; numerical confidence-interval endpoints and AI-arm SDs are not printed. This outcome concerns resemblance to an AI idea, not diversity across different people, and is coded with_ai/other. The screening form moved former outcome S1-O10 into its notes solely because of its outcome cap; the extraction specification has no such cap, so both contrasts are retained with form_outcome_id null. Supplement Section 3 specifies randomly sampling an AI idea generated for the same story topic, corroborating main PDF p. 5 and clarifying the conflicting same-condition wording on main PDF p. 8. Treatment means are not derived by adding coefficients to the printed control mean. The unadjusted model contains only assigned-condition indicators and a constant, so its printed Constant and parenthesized SE are recorded as the Human-only mean and its model-based SE. Treatment means are not computed from the constant and coefficient. Existing main-text p-values are retained. For otherwise missing p-values, significance symbols supply the printed upper bound and an unmarked coefficient leaves p_value null. The multi-regressor F-Stat is an omnibus model test and is not entered as a test of either individual AI-arm contrast. The Human-only SD comes from the full Human group in Table S12; statistics for the self-selected AI-use groups are not substituted for randomized AI arms. Table S11 prints the coefficient as 4.288, while the main text prints 4.29; the main-text value is retained, with the supplement precision documented here. Neither similarity outcome is listed in the complete preregistration, so preregistered_primary is no.

sample.notes: Counts are the printed people analyzed for this contrast. Counts are not inferred from study-wide totals or degrees of freedom. The people contributing to the rated projects are not enumerated, and project membership, team sizes, and team formation are not reported; participant counts for this analysis are therefore null. The student-level questionnaire/SEM counts cannot be substituted for project contributors. The article reports individual student allocation followed by instruction in separate classes by arm. The study assignment unit is session under extraction rule 9, despite the individual-allocation wording. The number of independent instructional clusters is unreported; the rated projects must not be used as cluster counts. Cluster replication required for core eligibility remains unconfirmed. The article does not establish whether the tabulated means use initial independent ratings or scores after discussion to consensus (PDF pp. 12, 20-21). Higher values mean better quality of the final design output, so higher_is is more_creative under the usefulness construct. Means, SDs, the t-test, and Cohen’s d are transcribed exactly as printed. The paper does not specify the standardizer for d. The independent-sample test treats projects as observations and reports no participant- or class-adjusted uncertainty, so se_basis is output. No mean difference, SE, or interval has been calculated. The composite is coded usefulness because it measures the quality of a creative design output (PDF p. 20, Section 4.6; codebook Section 6). Its output-level uncertainty and unresolved instructional-cluster replication remain limitations.

sample.notes: Counts are the printed people analyzed for this contrast. Counts are not inferred from study-wide totals or degrees of freedom. Bonferroni-adjusted Dunn pairwise p-value. This contrast uses entire randomized factorial cells at the same assigned task-factor level. No marginal effect, interaction or direct contrast between AI configurations was computed. sample.notes: Counts are the printed people analyzed for this contrast. Counts are not inferred from study-wide totals or degrees of freedom. This is the broad design-quality composite, coded usefulness; the Creativity rubric dimension is not separately reported. The analysis uses one design-achievement score per student; Table 1 reports participant counts and SDs, and sections 4-4.1 describe one-way ANOVA followed by Tukey HSD. The p_value is the printed pairwise Tukey bound. The reported F is an omnibus test across all study arms, so stats.test is null. The printed arm summaries and pairwise significance appear inconsistent; they are preserved without correction or calculation. No pair-specific total N is printed, so n_total is null rather than calculated from the arm counts. No numerical pairwise difference, SE, confidence interval, or standardized effect is printed. The artwork was produced with AI available in the AI arms and graded at course end; this is immediate assisted production, not a new delayed or unassisted task (PDF p. 9, section 3.5; PDF p. 11, section 5.1).

sample.notes: Counts are the printed people analyzed for this contrast. Counts are not inferred from study-wide totals or degrees of freedom. The eligible full-sample contrast is the same in Table 2 and the total-effect statement: High AI dependence is treatment and Low AI dependence is control, following the screening form. The positive printed t and Cohen’s d describe Low AI dependence minus High AI dependence, opposite to treatment minus control; their printed signs are retained. The printed total effect c is retained as the overall treatment contrast already represented in this record, not as an additional mediation estimate. The direct effect adjusted for critical thinking, the indirect effect, and its bootstrap interval are excluded; the indirect-effect interval must not be assigned to this total contrast. Figure 3 on PDF p. 7 has raster mediation-path labels inconsistent with the prose. Table 2 and the explicit total-effect sentence on PDF p. 6 supply the retained statistics; no figure-only number is recorded. Counts use the printed actual sample and per-group counts, not degrees of freedom; no exclusions or outcome-specific analyzed counts are separately reported. Both groups used ChatGPT while producing their scored AUT responses, supporting question=with_ai and outcome_with_ai=true. The design is between participants, so within_person=null. The averaged-rater creativity index is compared between people, supporting unit=participant, sd_level=participant, and se_basis=participant; the paper does not fully describe aggregation over individual ideas, rating dimensions, and the two AUT objects. The combined CAT index measures overall_creativity; higher scores indicate more_creative output. Expert-rater coding follows the trained psychology graduate raters and the description of the same measure as expert-rated on PDF p. 9. The contrast qualifies as ai_design because both arms use ChatGPT with different instructions. It also bundles different earlier priming experiences. High-dependence participants were instructed to adopt AI solutions directly, but people performed the task and submitted the scored responses, so this is not a model-only arm. The paper does not state the standardizer for Cohen’s d, and no SE or confidence interval is printed for the eligible overall contrast. All recorded numerical statistics are transcribed without calculation.

The source quote for n_total also preserves the complete Table 2 descriptive row, whose columns are Obs, Mean, Median, STD, P25, and P75. The rated and embedded comparisons include participants with at least one valid idea, a restriction after random assignment. Table 3 prints Difference 0.018 beside means 0.010 and -0.057; the printed difference is inconsistent with those means and is retained unchanged. PDF p. 20 gives the analysis counts, independently checked against PDF pp. 12 and 17. These are the main available-case arm comparisons, not the separate tool-user regressions. Reconciliation audit: PDF p. 9 describes one assigned tool beside the idea-submission form, confirming immediate output production with AI available in the treatment arm and a between-person contrast (outcome_with_ai=true; within_person=null).

F degrees of freedom, arm SDs/SEs, difference SEs/CIs, and standardized effects are not printed; none were derived. The source quote for n_total also preserves the complete Table 2 descriptive row, whose columns are Obs, Mean, Median, STD, P25, and P75. Its STD describes the combined analysis sample, not either arm or a within-arm pooled SD, and is not entered as an arm SD. Printed decimal precision is retained in the source quotes. The rated and embedded comparisons include participants with at least one valid idea, a restriction after random assignment. They are not complete intention-to-treat analyses (PDF pp. 12, 16, and 20). The paper calls this Divergent Thinking, but it compares ideas across participants and is coded diversity/across_people. The comparison pool is defined separately within each condition. It is unclear whether a participant's own other ideas or invalid ideas enter the reference pool. Table 2 repeats the Functional Appropriateness row verbatim for this outcome and has a negative overall mean incompatible with the positive arm means in Table 3; no corrected summary was inferred. The sentence on PDF p. 17 saying tool nonusers have missing divergence conflicts with Table 3: its divergence counts exceed its tool-user counts. The counts recorded here follow the outcome row. The ANOVA uses participant averages; it does not report an adjustment for their shared reference pools. Footnote 10 says TF-IDF embeddings yield consistent results but prints no separate arm levels or uncertainty. Reconciliation audit: PDF p. 17 defines one minus cosine similarity against other ideas within condition and then averages each participant’s idea scores. This confirms question=across_people, construct=diversity, unit=participant, and higher_is=more_diverse. PDF p. 20 supplies the outcome-specific analysis counts; its F test treats participant averages as observations. Reconciliation audit: PDF p. 9 describes one assigned tool beside the idea-submission form, confirming immediate output production with AI available in the treatment arm and a between-person contrast (outcome_with_ai=true; within_person=null).

sample.notes: Counts are the printed people analyzed for this contrast. Counts are not inferred from study-wide totals or degrees of freedom. The means are adjusted marginal means, and the F test is the Group / Creativity univariate test following MANCOVA. The covariates are prior ChatGPT use, Week 1 creativity, and Week 1 analytical skills (PDF p. 9, Results RQ2). The paper calls Week 1 scores baseline and describes baseline tasks as preceding intervention (PDF p. 5, Section 3.1), so this is retained as the reported baseline-adjusted contrast. The exact timing of Week 1 measurement relative to initial AI access remains unresolved because Table 1 places supported coursework in the opening weeks. The MANCOVA dependent variable's measurement occasion or aggregation is unspecified; this is not identified as a final-session score. The analysis is at the student level: Table 6 supplies analyzed student counts, not counts of ratings or submissions. The total is the main-study count printed in the abstract, whose arm counts match Table 6; it was not inferred from degrees of freedom. AI was available while the intervention products were made. Immediate identifies assessment during supported coursework; no outcome after AI withdrawal is reported. Students remained in separate instructional groups, so repeated assessments do not make this a within-person AI crossover. se_basis=participant describes the reported student-level analysis and does not establish valid precision for class randomization. No class-adjusted uncertainty, arm SD, mean difference, difference SE, or confidence interval is printed. No missing statistic was computed.

sample.notes: Counts are the printed people analyzed for this contrast. Counts are not inferred from study-wide totals or degrees of freedom. The mean and SE fields contain arm-specific latent mean slopes and their standard errors, not final creativity-score levels or a treatment-indicator regression coefficient. Results RQ1 explicitly compares growth across groups (PDF p. 8), so the reported arm parameters are retained as the descriptive slope comparison. No between-arm slope difference, difference SE, confidence interval, or test is printed. Table 3 prints < .000 for each arm parameter; those within-arm tests against zero are preserved in the source quote and are not a contrast p-value. Three-decimal table precision is preserved in that quote, including 0.210 and 0.010; rounded restatements in the prose are not additional estimates. No growth-model-specific analyzed participant count is printed, so n_treatment, n_control, and n_total are null. The latent growth factors describe individual students over repeated submissions, making participant the analysis unit and the reported uncertainty basis; no class effects or class-adjusted uncertainty are reported. Repeated measurement within each instructional group is not randomized crossover: within_person is null. AI remained available during the intervention, so this is with_ai, not after_ai. The time-step unit is unresolved: the procedure describes biweekly submissions across two semesters, while the figure labels occasions as weeks. No time conversion was made. Figure 1 has no numeric labels on the plotted points, and no occasion-specific means were read from the graph. Initial intercepts and random-factor variances were not treated as intervention effects or observed-score SDs.
